title: Cantiere Live
pitch: Cantiere Live: your quote editor and your AI agent, working the same page together — add materials, calculate margins, and finalize with one human click.
about_excerpt: Cantiere Live: your quote editor and your AI agent, working the same page together — add materials, calculate margins, and finalize with one human click. Like Comment Story Updates Inspiration Preparing a quote as an Italian artisan (idraulico, elettricista, termotecnico) is a daily, high-stakes task: search the price catalog, type rows, check your margin, get the IVA right. It's tedious, error-prone, and the agent can't easily help without "guessing" through a table. We wanted an app where the artisan and an AI agent build the same quote together — agent does the tedious work, human stays in charge. What it does Cantiere Live is a WebMCP-powered quote editor for Italian tradespeople. A human artisan sets the client and the applicable IVA regime (4% / 10% / 22% / flat-rate), edits rows, and reviews margins. An AI agent (via ChatGPT's in-app browser or Chrome with WebMCP) operates the same quote through typed WebMCP tools: search_materials , get_line_items , add_line_item , update_line_item , remove_line_item , get_quote_summary , and a read-only suggest_improvement advisor. Every agent action applies live, is highlighted and auto-scrolled into view, and can be undone with one click. The Assistant activity panel explains every action in plain language — including what was asked and why it couldn't be done . How we built it A Next.js 14 / React / TypeScript app with Tailwind CSS. Tools are registered on document.modelContext.registerTool(...) ( lib/webmcp-tools.ts ), backed by a spec-compliant polyfill ( lib/webmcp-polyfill.ts ) so the app works in any browser. We implement granular permissions via real AbortSignal revocation, dynamic context-scoped registration, structured recoverable errors ( { code, error, recoverable, suggestions[] } ), a user-facing activity feed ( lib/activity-summary.ts ), and per-line IVA with the Italian "beni di valore significativo" split ( lib/vat.ts ). We also expose a tool through the WebMCP Declarative API (a form the agent can pre-fill), demonstrating both APIs. Deployed on Vercel. Challenges we ran into Getting native WebMCP to activate on the deployed (HTTPS) origin — it's an Origin Trial, so the #enable-webmcp-testing flag alone isn't enough on Chrome Stable; we added the origin-trial token. Also making the activity log user-friendly (no tool names/JSON/timing) and ensuring the assistant is certain when a capability is turned off, instead of guessing from an error. Accomplishments that we're proud of A complete, coherent product experience — not a proof of concept. Both WebMCP APIs (imperative + declarative) with genuine, non-trivial implementations. Granular permissions that really unregister tools from document.modelContext via AbortSignal . Human-only finalization ( finalize_quote is never a tool) + one-click undo. Domain-accurate IVA per quote line (4/10/22% + significant-goods split + flat-rate). What we learned How WebMCP lets a web app declare structured tools so agents stop guessing, how Origin Trials gate native features on deployed origins, and how to design a human-in-the-loop experience that keeps the human in control without slowing the agent down. What's next for Cantiere Live More tools (batch discount, quote duplication), a quote history library the agent can search, deeper advisory capabilities (materials suggestion, margin coaching) and implement webMCP in our AiFatto app. Built With ai-agent chrome html javascript next.js openai react tailwind-css typescript vercel w3c-webmcp webmcp Try it out cantierelive.vercel.app github.com Submitted to The WebMCP Challenge Created by Diego Radoni Like Share this project: Updates Diego Radoni started this project — Sep 02, 2026 05:21 PM EDT
